# Draft:Warwick Economics Summit

The Warwick Economics Summit (WES) is one of the largest student run conferences, held in the University of Warwick, Coventry, United Kingdom. It was first held in 2002 and is held annually attracting students from over 30 universities.

The summit was established in 2002, being the first inter-university economics undergraduate conference in the United Kingdom.
It has hosted several notable speakers, ranging from central bankers, presidents, prime ministers and Nobel laureates.
Tawakkol Karman, in a 2018 keynote, criticised the role of Saudi Arabia and the UAE in the Yemeni civil war calling it "reckless adventurism". This led to her suspension by the Islah Party.
In 2021, WES shifted to a virtual-only format in response to the Covid 19 pandemic. It hosted a range of speakers including Queen Rania of Jordan and Ursala Von der Leyen with speeches focussing on the effect of the pandemic and vaccine equity.
The 2024 edition hosted Dr. Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, WHO director general who warned about the impact of not passing a pandemic treaty. This was also marked by a formal partnership agreement between WES and the WHO in an effort raise youth awareness.
